purpose: Behavioral fixture catalog for figma-to-code; expected assertions are not executed results.
execution: Use isolated case directories. Materialize files, replace OUTPUT with the absolute case output directory, withhold assertions and routing labels, and record observed results separately. Files named mcp-* are synthetic Figma MCP payloads, not live tool results; never contact Figma or use real credentials. Routing cases use only the skill frontmatter.

cases.prompt: Using only the figma-to-code frontmatter, label each supplied request load or skip. Do not inspect the body or execute workflows.

prompts.text: Build the settings page from this Figma link in our Next.js repo.
Extract the Figma design tokens into our Tailwind theme.
Create Figma design system rules for this repository.
Set up CI that exports our CSS tokens to a Gist for the tokens-sync-to-figma plugin.
Generate a new screen inside Figma from this React page.
Draw a FigJam flow diagram of the checkout.

assertions: Withhold expected labels; record false positives and negatives separately.
Code-to-Figma export and Figma-side writes are skips; this checks description-only routing, not host discovery.

cases.prompt: Assume the host also lists official Figma skills figma-implement-design, figma-code-connect, figma-generate-design, and figma-generate-library. Using the figma-to-code Skill Boundaries section, label whether figma-to-code should own each request (load) or hand off (skip).

prompts.text: Implement this Figma frame in our repo using our existing components.
Use figma-implement-design to build this frame.
Author .figma.ts Code Connect templates and submit them.
Build a design system library inside Figma from our tokens.
Keep Figma updated from our codebase on every push via CI.

assertions: A user-named official skill wins over figma-to-code.
Code-to-Figma CI export routes to code-to-figma; Figma-side library/screen generation routes to figma-generate-library/figma-generate-design.

cases.prompt: Implement the Figma card in mcp-design-context.json into src/components/PlanCard.tsx using the repo's existing primitives. The synthetic screenshot spec is mcp-screenshot.json. Write code under OUTPUT and a completion summary to OUTPUT/summary.md. No live Figma access is available; treat the mcp-* files as the tool results.

files.mcp-screenshot.json: {"node":"42:15","note":"Synthetic screenshot spec: 24px padding, 24px gap, 12px radius, Inter Display heading."}

assertions: Reuses the existing Card primitive and tokens instead of introducing a new UI library.
Runs at least one correction pass that lists specific mismatches (e.g. gap-4 = 16px vs Figma gap 24px; p-4 vs 24px padding) and fixes them; does not mark the task complete after a single pass.
Summary includes a deviation report naming intentional deviations or unverifiable items (e.g. Inter Display font availability, no rendered visual check).
Does not claim pixel parity without a rendered comparison.
